[S1] Metformin: general information

Metformin is a prescription medicine commonly used for type 2 diabetes. It helps lower blood glucose. Treatment and monitoring depend on the individual and their other medicines and conditions. A clinician or pharmacist should advise on suitability or treatment changes. This educational summary does not recommend starting, stopping or changing a prescription.

[S2] Metformin: possible side effects

Metformin can cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort, reduced appetite and altered taste. Vitamin B12 deficiency is another possible issue. Not everyone experiences side effects. Persistent or troublesome effects need a pharmacist or doctor. Rare serious problems include lactic acidosis and severe allergy; severe illness or breathing problems require urgent assessment. [S1] Cetirizine: allergies and possible side effects

Cetirizine is an antihistamine used for allergy symptoms such as hay fever and hives. Although classed as a less-drowsy antihistamine, it can still cause sleepiness. Other possible common effects include headache, dry mouth, nausea, dizziness and diarrhoea. Do not drive if it makes you sleepy. Check the leaflet and ask a pharmacist about suitability. Brand names are not enough to identify an ingredient because different products in a brand family may contain different medicines.
